title: CONUS Monthly Atlas

initial_product.intended_interface: Interactive map with component layers and evidence quality
initial_product.vehicle_performance_model: Not implemented or validated in this package

overview_grid.aggregation: 2×2 native cells weighted by spherical area; contributors with a complete 20-year record only
overview_grid.status: Implemented first overview grid; future inputs retain separate native support
overview_grid.change_from_starter: The proposed 4 km EPSG:5070 engineering default was replaced for this first release by a documented NOAA geographic source grid and an approximately 9 km display. No artificial 4 km precision is claimed.

initial_product.primary_land_state_source: Not acquired; NLDAS and soil survey products remain documented candidates

elevation_context.method: Systematic sampling; static context, not a monthly mean

spatial_support_policy.overview: Retain the documented climate and relief grids without adding artificial local precision.
spatial_support_policy.local_features: Inspect mapped water geometry and bridge inventory points separately at local zoom. Inventory coordinates are not precise bridge outlines or verified shoreline connections.
spatial_support_policy.hydrology: Selected calendar month historical discharge estimates apply only at gauges. No spatial interpolation.
spatial_support_policy.display_zoom: Magnification does not increase the information or positional accuracy of source data.
spatial_support_policy.land_cover: The national overview preserves coarse provider classes at about 4–7 km spacing. Local detail separately retrieves imagery resampled from native 30 m USGS cells and queries raw classes at nominal 30 m support. Neither display zoom nor resampling adds source detail.
spatial_support_policy.hydrography: National river/lake context is generalized at 1:10,000,000 cartographic scale. Local Overture water geometry is separate. Symbol width, geometry and imagery do not establish water conditions.
spatial_support_policy.seasonal_overlays: Seasonal land snow and Great Lakes surface ice are separate selectable overlays, independent of the mapped land-cover type and static 2025 NLCD perennial ice/snow. Overlay cells retain source support, not per-pixel certainty.
spatial_support_policy.regional_slope: 500 m input samples (nominally 1.5 km 3×3 footprint); 0.05° display cells, roughly 5.6 km north–south, narrower east–west. Albers grid distances have small projection scale variation. No local grade or current condition inferred.

environmental_water.missing_year_policy: Retain nulls and explicitly identify partial baselines; no imputation.

local_detail.source: USGS Annual NLCD 2025 imagery, Overture experimental base-water vectors, FHWA 2025 bridge locations and USGS historical gauges
local_detail.release_discovery: Current STAC release on load, validated water layer, explicit dated fallback or service failure
context: 2025 land cover from 30 m source with independent opacity and visibility controls
local_detail.geometry_meaning: Source water geometry and dated bridge points; no current water condition, water-crossing assertion or suitability inference.

land_cover.source: USGS Annual NLCD Collection 1.2 · MRLC raw WCS
land_cover.display_support: Coarse categorical service overview; approximately 4–7 km spacing; local composition unknown
land_cover.method: Request 2025 raw class-valued GeoTIFF from the official USGS MRLC WCS at 1180 × 520 pixels with nearest-neighbor interpolation. Use the returned affine coordinates, not the requested bounding box, because server reprojection expands the extent. Read integer band values directly, retain provider palette labels, and convert NoData 250 to null. Preserve the valid USGS CONUS footprint including inland and coastal water; use 2025 Census outlines as reference only. No color decoding, class averaging, gap filling, area-majority inference, or mobility scoring.
land_cover.interpretation: Categorical landscape context; no difficulty weights, local vegetation-structure estimate or monthly state inference
land_cover.spatial_footprint: All valid USGS CONUS source cells including mapped inland/coastal water; Census land outlines are reference-only

local_detail.service: Official USGS MRLC WMS GetMap and raw GetFeatureInfo
local_detail.display: Provider WMS imagery resampled from 30 m source cells. Zooming or smaller rendered pixels do not add information below the source support.
local_detail.failed_local_query_policy: Show unavailable or unknown; never substitute the coarse overview

bridges.source: FHWA National Bridge Inventory — 2025 highway bridge locations
bridges.display: Individual inventory points and lazy per-state descriptions in local detail only. No bridge symbols or counts in the national overview.
bridges.interpretation: Not every record crosses water. Locations and descriptions do not establish current availability, suitability or an exact bridge outline.

national_water_context.scope: Contiguous-US map extent including adjacent Canada and Mexico for geographic context; all five Great Lakes are retained.
national_water_context.symbol_policy: River lines are cartographic symbols with unmeasured widths; supplied intermittent class is dashed

location_evidence_panel.scope: Selected overview cell, not statewide aggregation

calendar.snow_permanent_class_policy: Retain 2025 NLCD perennial ice/snow as a base class. Seasonal overlay choices do not recode it.

seasonal_snow.title: Seasonal snow on land
seasonal_snow.source: US National Ice Center IMS daily snow and ice analyses; distributed via NSIDC (G02156)
seasonal_snow.quantity: Frequency of snow-covered land days, as a percentage
seasonal_snow.temporal_support: Each calendar month in 2006–2025; analysis dates, not the next-day filenames
seasonal_snow.spatial_support: Nominal 24 km IMS grid; nearest source cell at 0.25-degree overview cell centers
seasonal_snow.calculation: For each calendar month and year, divide snow days by valid snow-covered or snow-free land days. Require valid land observations on at least 80% of the calendar days and all 20 qualifying years. Average the 20 annual percentages equally. Water, ice and unknown flags do not count as snow-free land.
seasonal_snow.limitations: Values are frequencies, not snow depth, snow-water equivalent, snowpack strength, snowfall totals or current conditions. Null and valid 0% remain distinct.

seasonal_surface_ice.title: Seasonal Great Lakes surface ice
seasonal_surface_ice.source: NOAA GLERL Great Lakes Ice Cover Database (USNIC/CIS charts)
seasonal_surface_ice.geographic_scope: Lake Superior, Michigan, Huron, Erie, Ontario and Lake Saint Clair; no general inland-river or nationwide water-ice layer
seasonal_surface_ice.temporal_support: Each calendar month in 2006–2025; use years with enough charted days, retain count at each cell
seasonal_surface_ice.spatial_support: 1024 × 1024 Mercator source grid; projection cell size 1,800 m. The source coordinate package supplies latitudes, longitudes, and lake IDs. 0.05° geographic overview; nearest source grid cell to each displayed cell center, masked by the NOAA lake IDs.
seasonal_surface_ice.calculation: Average valid concentration (0–100%) across available chart dates within each calendar month and year. Include a cell-year only with valid values on at least 80% of all calendar days. Equally average qualifying yearly means if at least 10 of 20 years qualify. Retain actual qualifying year counts.
seasonal_surface_ice.observed_coverage: Qualifying values occur in December–April. May, June and November have some chart dates without sufficient qualifying years. July–October have no archive chart dates in this baseline.
seasonal_surface_ice.limitations: Missing is never ice-free; 0% is a valid charted estimate. Surface concentration is not thickness, ice strength or current status.

regional_mean_slope.title: Regional mean terrain slope (degrees)
regional_mean_slope.temporal_support: Static terrain; DEM vintage varies across source coverage.
regional_mean_slope.spatial_support: 500 m input samples (nominally 1.5 km 3×3 footprint); 0.05° display cells, roughly 5.6 km north–south, narrower east–west. Albers grid distances have small projection scale variation. No local grade or current condition inferred.
regional_mean_slope.calculation: Request 500 m elevation samples in NAD83 / CONUS Albers, EPSG:5070 with bilinear interpolation and a one-sample halo around each tile. Calculate Horn 3×3 horizontal gradient from metre-based vertical and horizontal units; require all nine samples valid. Angle is atan(hypot(dz/dx,dz/dy)) in degrees. GDAL average resampling across valid contributing slope values gives each 0.05° overview cell. Clip centers to bundled contiguous-state boundaries and exclude generalized mapped lake centers. This is not slope computed from the 11 km ETOPO elevation overlay.
regional_mean_slope.limitations: A regional mean angle; not within-cell peak slope, local or trail grade, roughness, aspect, or a vehicle traversal assessment.

temporal_contract.interpretation: Twelve calendar-month climatologies, with separately dated landscape and infrastructure records.
temporal_contract.landscape_date_policy: Record release, acquisition/snapshot date and freshness limits separately; do not assume every layer is current
temporal_contract.climate_period_policy: Use the same calendar month in each of 2006–2025. Require 20 years at a contributing native climate cell.
temporal_contract.precipitation: Average the 20 respective monthly precipitation totals with equal year weights.
temporal_contract.state_variables: Form monthly summaries from quality-controlled samples; retain year counts and between-year variability
temporal_contract.completeness_policy: Strict complete-record target; incomplete values remain flagged and are not silently substituted
temporal_contract.antecedent_conditions: No daily event or antecedent soil-moisture conditions are derived from monthly totals.
temporal_contract.extremes_policy: Retain daily or subdaily source information where needed; a monthly mean is not an estimate of extreme exposure

rules: Source availability is not the same as downloaded or validated data.
Missing values are not zero and are not easy terrain.
Water is a mapped surface class, not a missing-data category.
Absence of a mapped feature does not prove physical absence.
Resampling does not increase the independent information in a source.
Do not assign a numerical confidence probability without calibration evidence.

exterior_exposure_layer.status: Monthly exterior air temperature and precipitation available; humidity, wind and solar pending

scenarios.assumption: Fitted climate controls operate; residual heat and thermal inadequacy remain possible.
One or more climate-control functions perform below normal capability.
Active crew heating and cooling unavailable; ventilation state is unspecified.

scenario_rules: Operating controls do not guarantee a comfortable cabin.
Cold-weather loss of heating must be considered as well as loss of cooling.
Control failure does not imply that the cabin instantly equals outdoor temperature.
Ventilation availability must not be inferred solely from heating or cooling failure.
Do not assume a failure rate, arbitrary cooling loss percentage, or universal temperature offset.
Keep scenarios separate unless evidence supports probability weights.

drinking_water.user_requirement: Do not assume planned logistical resupply remains available.

scenarios.meaning: Usable drinking-water supply is assumed available; quantity and duration are not inferred.
Resupply is assumed interrupted; existing usable supply remains unknown.
Available usable water and resupply status have not been established.

rules: Mapped water, rainfall and soil wetness do not establish safe drinking-water availability.
An identified source does not establish its quality, treatment or actual accessibility.
Keep supplied water and environmental surface water separate.
Do not assign failure probabilities, consumption rates or endurance estimates without evidence.
Do not combine these uncalibrated scenarios into terrain or crew scores.
drinking_water.scope: Crew drinking-water supply only; separate from mapped environmental water and physical landscape indicators.
